name: grok
specialty: Different model family: builds, reviews, and gives independent second opinions that catch blind spots.
notes: In headless `grok -p`, tools that need approval are auto-denied; the run ends with "permission required: ... was not run, as a headless run cannot ask for approval". Grant what a seat needs with --permission-mode and --allow up front.
acceptEdits alone still blocked Edit in headless mode; builders also need --allow Edit --allow Write.

Plan mode does not carry into subagents (each starts with its own plan-mode state and inherits the permission mode), and allow rules are merged from ~/.claude/settings.json, the repo's .claude/settings.json and ~/.grok/config.toml. So every seat passes explicit deny rules (deny beats any allow) and --no-subagents: the reviewer denies Bash, Edit, Write and MCPTool; the builder denies Bash, MCPTool, Edit(.git/**) and Write(.git/**), because a hook written under .git is shell by proxy.
Builders get no shell (--deny Bash): the lead runs tests and commits.
Status: grok version. Models: grok models (grok-4.7, grok-4.7-build-fast, grok-4.6, grok-4.5).
The prompt goes in a file (--prompt-file {promptFile}); the brief or diff never enters the command line.

--no-subagents does not stop background workflows (the workflow tool, .grok/workflows scripts, /deep-research), which are on by default and not gated by plan mode, so every seat runs with GROK_WORKFLOWS=0 (profile env; roster.py command prefixes the shell line with env GROK_WORKFLOWS=0).
